May 28, 2026


# Bone Graft Dental: Your Complete 2026 Guide to Procedure, Recovery & Costs


For many patients, hearing the words "you need a bone graft" can be an unexpected and unsettling moment in their dental journey. Whether you are considering dental implants to replace missing teeth or addressing bone loss from gum disease, understanding the foundation of your oral health is critical. At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery, we have spent over 50 years helping patients restore not just their smiles, but the underlying structure that supports them.

A dental bone graft is, in essence, a procedure to rebuild the scaffolding of your jaw. Just as a house requires a solid concrete foundation before walls can be erected, dental implants require sufficient bone density and volume to remain stable and functional for a lifetime. Without this foundation, implants can fail, and facial aesthetics can change prematurely.

While the concept of surgery may seem daunting, modern bone grafting is a routine, predictable, and highly successful procedure. In this comprehensive guide, updated for 2026, we will walk you through everything you need to know—from the different types of grafts and materials used to the costs you can expect and the recovery process. Our goal is to replace anxiety with knowledge, empowering you to make the best decision for your long-term oral health.


## What Is a Dental Bone Graft and Why Do You Need One?


A dental bone graft is a surgical procedure that adds volume and density to your jaw in areas where bone loss has occurred. The graft material acts as a scaffold, stimulating your body to regenerate its own bone tissue over time. Eventually, the graft material is replaced by your own natural bone, creating a strong base for dental restorations.


### Understanding Jawbone Loss and Its Consequences


Your jawbone preserves its strength through the pressure exerted by chewing. When a tooth is lost, that stimulation disappears, and the body begins to resorb (break down) the bone in that area. In fact, the alveolar bone can lose up to 25% of its height in the first year after tooth extraction, with width loss being even more dramatic—studies show 40-60% of bone width can be lost within the first three years. Beyond the inability to place implants, significant bone loss can lead to a "sunken" facial appearance, premature aging, and shifting of remaining teeth.


### How Bone Grafts Prepare Your Jaw for Dental Implants


Dental implants are titanium posts that serve as artificial tooth roots. For an implant to osseointegrate (fuse) successfully, it must be completely surrounded by healthy bone. If your jaw is too thin or too soft, the implant will not be stable. A bone graft builds up the height and width of the jaw ridge, ensuring there is enough bone mass to anchor the implant securely.


### Who Is a Candidate for Dental Bone Grafting?


Almost anyone with missing teeth who wants dental implants is a potential candidate. You may require a graft if you have:

Had a tooth extracted recently or many years ago.

Experienced gum disease (periodontitis) that destroyed bone support.

Suffered trauma or injury to the jaw.

Developmental defects in the jaw.

Worn dentures for many years, leading to ridge atrophy.


## What Are the Different Types of Dental Bone Grafts?


Not all bone grafts are the same. The specific procedure recommended by your surgeon depends on the location of the bone loss, the severity of the defect, and your future treatment goals. Below is a comparison of the most common procedures performed in 2026.

Type

Purpose

Healing Time

Socket Preservation

Placed immediately after tooth extraction to prevent the socket from collapsing.

3-4 months

Ridge Augmentation

Builds up the width and height of the jaw ridge where bone has already receded.

4-6 months

Sinus Lift

Adds bone to the upper jaw by lifting the sinus membrane to create space for implants.

4-9 months

Block Graft

Uses a solid block of bone (usually autograft) for major reconstruction of large defects.

6-12 months


## What Materials Are Used in Dental Bone Grafts?


The material used for the graft is just as important as the technique. While using your own bone was once the only option, modern dentistry offers several effective alternatives that spare you from a second surgical site. According to the FDA, bone grafting materials marketed in the U.S. must demonstrate safety and effectiveness before receiving clearance — a requirement that applies to synthetic grafts, allografts, and xenografts alike.

Material

Source

Success Rate

Pros

Cons

Autograft

Your own bone (chin, hip, shin)

95-100%

Gold standard; contains your own live cells; zero rejection risk.

Requires a second surgical site; more post-op pain.

Allograft

Human donor (cadaver)

90-95%

No second surgery site; readily available; highly successful.

Processed to remove cells, so it acts only as a scaffold.

Xenograft

Animal (usually bovine/cow)

85-95%

Excellent structural stability; cost-effective.

Resorbs very slowly; some patients have ethical concerns.

Alloplastic

Synthetic (calcium phosphate)

80-90%

Unlimited supply; zero risk of disease transmission.

Lower regenerative potential compared to natural bone.


## How Is Dental Bone Graft Surgery Performed?


At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery, we prioritize patient comfort and precision. A typical bone graft procedure takes between one to three hours, depending on complexity.

Pre-Surgical Planning: We utilize advanced CBCT (3D imaging) to measure your exact bone density and visualize the anatomy of nerves and sinuses.

Anesthesia: You will be given anesthesia to ensure the procedure is painless. Options range from local anesthesia (numbing the area) to IV sedation or general anesthesia for more complex cases or anxious patients.

The Procedure: The surgeon makes a small incision in the gum tissue to expose the underlying bone. The graft material is packed into the defect. Often, a collagen membrane is placed over the graft to hold it in shape and prevent gum tissue from growing into the bone site.

Closure: The gum tissue is repositioned and stitched closed. In many cases, the graft is allowed to heal for several months before an implant is placed.


## What Is a Sinus Lift Procedure?


The upper jaw (maxilla) presents a unique challenge because the maxillary sinuses—air-filled pockets behind your cheeks—sit just above the roots of your upper back teeth. When these teeth are lost, the sinus floor often drops, leaving a paper-thin layer of bone that cannot support an implant.

A sinus lift is a specialized bone graft procedure where the surgeon gently lifts the sinus membrane upward and packs bone graft material underneath it. This effectively raises the "floor" of the sinus, creating sufficient vertical bone height for an implant.

Lateral Window Approach: Used for significant bone loss. A small window is made in the side of the jaw bone to access the sinus.

Crestal Approach (Osteotome): A less invasive technique used when only a small amount of bone is needed; the floor is lifted through the hole prepared for the implant.


## What Can You Expect During Bone Graft Recovery?


Recovery is generally manageable, but patience is required. Bone regeneration is a biological process that cannot be rushed. Here is a timeline of what you can expect:

Timeframe

What's Happening

What You'll Experience

Days 1-3

Initial healing and clotting.

Swelling, bruising, and soreness are at their peak. Minor bleeding is normal.

Week 1-2

Soft tissue (gum) healing.

Swelling subsides significantly. Stitches may dissolve or be removed. Mild discomfort.

Month 1-3

Bone integration begins.

You should feel normal. The graft is organizing and beginning to fuse with natural bone.

Month 3-6

Graft maturation.

The graft becomes dense enough to support an implant. X-rays will confirm density.

Month 6-12

Complete remodeling.

For major grafts, this is when the bone achieves maximum strength for implant loading.

Insurance Coverage: It is important to note that most dental insurance plans consider bone grafts to be a specialized procedure and may not cover the full cost. However, if the bone loss is due to trauma, pathology (like a cyst), or a medical condition, medical insurance may occasionally provide coverage. We recommend checking with our financial coordinators to explore your benefits and financing options, such as CareCredit, which can break the cost into manageable monthly payments.


## What Is the Success Rate of Dental Bone Grafts?


Dental bone grafting is one of the most successful surgical procedures in dentistry. Success rates generally range from 90% to 100%.

The primary indicators of a successful graft are the lack of infection, proper wound closure, and radiographic evidence that the bone density has increased. When a bone graft heals correctly, it significantly increases the survival rate of the subsequent dental implant, often pushing implant success rates above 97%.


## Is a Dental Bone Graft Painful?


This is the most common question we hear. During the procedure itself, you will feel absolutely no pain due to effective local anesthesia and sedation options. You may feel vibration or pressure, but not sharpness or pain.

Post-Operative Management: After the anesthesia wears off, most patients experience moderate soreness rather than acute pain. This is typically managed effectively with over-the-counter anti-inflammatories (like ibuprofen) and Tylenol. For more complex grafts, we may prescribe a short course of stronger pain medication. Most patients find that the significant discomfort fades within 3 to 5 days.


## What Should You Eat After Bone Graft Surgery?


Proper nutrition is vital for healing, but you must protect the surgical site from trauma.

Days 1-7 (Soft/Liquid Diet): Stick to cool or lukewarm foods. Yogurt, smoothies (no straws!), applesauce, mashed potatoes, scrambled eggs, and protein shakes. Avoid anything hot, spicy, or acidic.

Week 2-4 (Transitional Foods): You can introduce soft pasta, fish, steamed vegetables, and oatmeal. Continue to chew away from the surgical site.

Foods to Avoid: Popcorn, nuts, chips, seeds, and hard candies must be avoided for several weeks, as sharp particles can lodge in the gum tissue and cause infection.

Nutritional Requirements: Ensure you are getting enough protein, Calcium, and Vitamin D, as these are the building blocks of new bone.


## What Are the Risks and Complications?


While rare, complications can occur. Being aware of them helps in early detection and treatment.

Infection: Signs include increasing pain after day 3, fever, foul taste/odor, or pus.

Graft Failure: Occurs in approximately 2-10% of cases in the general healthy population. However, smokers and patients with uncontrolled diabetes face significantly higher failure rates (10-20%). The graft material may come loose or fail to integrate.

Nerve Irritation: Temporary numbness in the chin or lip can occur if the graft is near the lower jaw nerve, though this usually resolves with time.

Sinus Issues: After a sinus lift, minor congestion is normal, but severe pressure should be reported.

If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact our office immediately. Early intervention can often save a graft.


## Are There Alternatives to Bone Grafting?


In some cases, patients may wish to avoid bone grafting entirely. Advances in implant technology have provided some alternatives:

Zygomatic Implants: These long implants anchor into the cheekbone (zygoma) rather than the jawbone, bypassing the need for grafting in the upper jaw.

All-on-4® Implants: This technique uses tilted implants to maximize contact with available bone, often avoiding the need for sinus lifts or extensive grafting.

Short Implants: In specific scenarios, shorter, wider implants may be used in areas with limited vertical bone height.

Traditional Bridges or Dentures: These restore aesthetics and some function without surgery, though they do not prevent further bone loss.


## How Do You Prepare for Bone Graft Surgery?


Preparation is key to a smooth surgery and recovery.

Medications: Provide a full list of medications. You may need to pause blood thinners under your physician's guidance.

Smoking: If you smoke, you must stop at least 2-4 weeks prior to surgery. Smoking restricts blood flow and is the number one cause of graft failure.

Logistics: If you are undergoing sedation, arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home.

Clothing: Wear loose, comfortable clothing with short sleeves for easy IV access.


## Special Considerations for Different Patients


Diabetic Patients: Uncontrolled blood sugar can impair healing. It is crucial to have your HbA1c levels under control before surgery.

Smokers: As mentioned, smoking poses a severe risk. We strongly advise cessation programs to protect your investment in your oral health.

Osteoporosis Patients: While osteoporosis affects body bones, it doesn't always rule out dental grafts. However, patients on bisphosphonate medications need a special evaluation to avoid complications like osteonecrosis.

Age Considerations: There is no upper age limit for bone grafting. As long as you are generally healthy, you can be a candidate. Conversely, young patients must wait until jaw growth is complete (usually late teens) before receiving implants.


## Making the Right Decision for Your Oral Health


A dental bone graft is an investment in your future. It provides the stability required to eat, speak, and smile with confidence. While the process involves time and healing, the result is a restored foundation that can last a lifetime.

With over 50 years of experience, Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery is dedicated to providing safe, expert care tailored to your unique anatomy. We understand that every patient's needs are different, and we are here to answer your questions honestly and clearly.

If you suspect you have bone loss or are considering dental implants, do not let fear of the unknown hold you back. Schedule a consultation today to discuss your options and build a plan for a healthier, stronger smile.

May 28, 2026


# TMJ Surgery: Treatment Options & Recovery


Jaw pain that doesn't quit. A click every time you open your mouth. A joint that locks mid-yawn and takes a terrifying few seconds to release. If any of that sounds familiar, you've probably already tried a mouthguard, maybe some physical therapy, possibly a round of anti-inflammatories — and you're still here, reading this, because nothing has fully worked.

That puts you in a specific and understandable place. Not everyone with a TMJ disorder needs surgery — research consistently shows that between 75% and 90% of cases improve with conservative, non-surgical care. But for the people who don't respond, surgery isn't a failure. It's the next logical step — and when it's the right call, the outcomes can be genuinely life-changing.

This guide covers every TMJ surgery type available today, what recovery actually looks like week by week, and how to know if you're a candidate. For patients whose TMJ disorder involves jaw misalignment, it's also worth knowing that TMJ procedures are sometimes combined with orthognathic (jaw) surgery — a corrective approach that repositions the upper and lower jaws for both functional and structural improvement.


## What Is TMJ Surgery — and Who Actually Needs It?


The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is the hinge that connects your jaw to your skull, just in front of each ear. It's one of the most complex joints in the human body — capable of moving in three directions simultaneously, every time you talk, chew, or yawn. When it breaks down, the effects ripple outward: jaw pain, ear pressure, chronic headaches, difficulty eating, and in severe cases, a joint that locks open or closed.

TMJ disorders are remarkably common. The TMJ Association estimates that anywhere from 10 to over 35 million Americans are affected at any given time — a wide range that reflects genuine uncertainty in the research, since large-scale population studies are difficult to conduct. What's consistent across the data is that women bear the heaviest burden: among those with major jaw limitations and chronic, unrelenting pain, women outnumber men nearly nine to one.

Surgery enters the picture when:

Conservative treatments — splints, physical therapy, medications, injections — have been tried and genuinely haven't provided lasting relief

Imaging confirms structural damage such as a displaced disc, bone deterioration, or joint adhesions that won't resolve on their own

The jaw is locking or causing enough dysfunction to significantly impact daily life

There's an underlying anatomical problem, like severe joint degeneration or ankylosis, that has a structural cause requiring a structural solution

If you haven't yet exhausted conservative options, surgery almost certainly isn't what your surgeon will recommend first. But if you have, the following procedures represent your real-world path forward.


## TMJ Surgery Treatment Options: From Least to Most Invasive



### Arthrocentesis — No Incision, No Camera, Maximum Simplicity


Arthrocentesis is the most minimally invasive TMJ surgery option. No incisions, no stitches — just two small needles placed in front of the ear to flush the joint with sterile fluid. That fluid washes out inflammatory byproducts, breaks up adhesions, and relieves the pressure that causes stiffness and pain.

It's typically performed under local anesthesia or light IV sedation, often in an office setting, and you go home the same day. Recovery is measured in days, not weeks. The National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research notes that arthrocentesis has been shown to improve jaw opening and help with pain relief, particularly when a displaced disc is involved.

Best for: Patients with early-to-moderate TMJ dysfunction, disc displacement, or joint stiffness that hasn't resolved with conservative treatment.


### TMJ Arthroscopy — Camera-Guided, Minimally Invasive, Same-Day


Arthroscopy takes the next step. A small incision in front of the ear allows a thin tube (cannula) to be inserted into the joint, through which a miniature camera (arthroscope) is threaded. The surgeon sees the inside of the joint on a screen in real time — and using small instruments through the same or adjacent port, can remove inflamed tissue, break up scar adhesions, reposition the articular disc, or flush the joint under direct visualization.

This is more precise than arthrocentesis because the surgeon can both diagnose and treat simultaneously. It requires general anesthesia or deep IV sedation and must be performed in a surgical center or hospital, but remains an outpatient procedure for most patients.

The long-term data is reassuring. A 10-year outcome study on arthroscopic TMJ surgery found an overall success rate of 83.8%, with pain scores dropping from significant levels to near-zero at the decade mark. That's not a temporary fix — that's a durable track record. A separate study tracking nearly 220 joints over an average of 6.9 years found that 77.7% of patients treated with arthroscopic lavage required no further surgery in the years that followed, though patients with the most advanced joint disease consistently needed escalation to open surgery.

Recovery timeline for arthroscopy:

Timeframe

What to Expect

Days 1–3

Mild soreness, possible ear ache, bite may feel slightly off

Week 1

Most patients return to desk work; soft diet continues

Weeks 2–4

Jaw exercises begin; progressive return to normal activities

Month 2+

Most patients back to normal eating and full jaw function

Best for: Patients who haven't responded to arthrocentesis, or who have moderate internal derangement confirmed on imaging.


### Open-Joint Surgery (Arthroplasty) — Direct Access for Structural Problems


When the joint has structural damage that a camera and small instruments can't fully address, open surgery becomes necessary. A longer incision is made along the natural border of the earlobe to give the surgeon direct visual and physical access to the joint itself.

Through this approach, the surgeon can remove bone spurs or excess bone growth, repair or reposition a damaged disc, remove scar tissue, or perform a discectomy when the disc is beyond repair. This is performed under general anesthesia, and some patients require an overnight hospital stay depending on the extent of the procedure.

Recovery takes longer — typically 2 to 6 weeks for initial healing — but the outcomes remain strong. Current evidence on open TMJ arthroplasty points to success rates around 80% when surgery is appropriately matched to the patient's specific joint pathology. Physical therapy is almost always part of the recovery plan after open surgery, with jaw mobility exercises typically beginning within the first two weeks.

Recovery timeline for open arthroplasty:

Liquid/soft diet, wound care, rest; incision area will be tender

Weeks 2–3

Jaw exercises begin; swelling reduces progressively

Weeks 4–6

Bone and tissue healing continues; diet gradually expands

Months 2–3

Most patients approaching full function with continued PT

Best for: Patients with structural joint damage — bone spurs, severely displaced or perforated discs, adhesions — that arthroscopy cannot adequately address.


### Total Joint Replacement — When the Joint Needs to Be Rebuilt


Total temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is reserved for end-stage cases: severe joint degeneration, ankylosis (where the joint has fused), failed prior surgeries, or conditions like advanced osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis that have destroyed the joint architecture. The natural joint is removed and replaced with a prosthetic implant — typically titanium and high-density polyethylene — engineered to replicate the joint's full range of function.

Modern total joint replacement can be customized using 3D imaging and digital jaw models, allowing surgeons to fabricate a prosthesis matched precisely to the patient's anatomy. Two incisions are required: one for the component attached to the skull, and one for the component fixed to the lower jaw.

The outcomes data for appropriately selected candidates is among the most compelling in the entire field. A 2025 systematic review covering 64 studies and nearly 2,400 patients found that total joint replacement consistently delivered 75–87% pain reduction and a 97% prosthesis survival rate, with average improvements in mouth opening of 26–36mm. That data spans patients with osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthritis, ankylosis, trauma, and idiopathic condylar resorption across physical, social, and psychological quality-of-life domains.

Recovery timeline for total joint replacement:

Days 1–5

Hospital or closely supervised recovery; liquid diet only

Weeks 1–3

Wound care, initial jaw exercises, prescribed pain management

Weeks 3–6

Progressive soft diet; physical therapy ramps up significantly

Months 2–3+

Full recovery; most patients report major quality-of-life improvement

Best for: End-stage joint disease where no other surgical option can adequately restore function.


## Jaw Surgery Recovery: What to Expect Across All Procedures


Here's the full picture, side by side:

Surgery Type

Recovery Window

Diet Restriction

Typical Work Return

Arthrocentesis

1–2 days

Soft foods 1–3 days

Next day (desk jobs)

Arthroscopy

1–2 weeks

Soft diet 2–4 weeks

3–5 days

Open Arthroplasty

2–6 weeks

Liquid then soft, 6–8 weeks

2–4 weeks

Total Joint Replacement

6–12 weeks

Liquid then progressive

4–6 weeks

A few recovery principles apply across all TMJ surgery types:

Jaw movement is essential, even early on. Counter-intuitively, keeping the jaw completely still leads to worse outcomes. Gentle range-of-motion exercises, prescribed by your surgeon, typically begin within the first one to two weeks.

Physical therapy is not optional after open surgery. It's a core part of recovery — not an add-on. Most surgeons refer patients to a therapist who specializes in jaw rehabilitation.

Sleep position matters. Sleep on your back or on the side opposite the surgery. Avoid pressure on the jaw during the first several weeks.

Follow-up appointments are built into recovery. Expect visits at roughly 1 week, 2–3 weeks, and 6 weeks post-surgery, with intervals adjusted from there based on your progress.


## Is TMJ Surgery Worth It? What the Research Actually Shows


This is the question most patients are really asking — not "what are the procedure names" but "will it actually fix things, and will I regret it?"

The long-term data is more reassuring than most people expect. A study that tracked TMJ surgery patients for more than two decades — 24 to 33 years post-operation — found that 87% were still satisfied with their results, with significant improvements in locking, clicking, and chewing pain maintained throughout. That's not temporary relief. That's a lasting outcome for the right patients.

It's also worth being honest about what surgery isn't: it's not a guaranteed cure, and it doesn't work equally well for all conditions. The TMJ Association is clear that there are still no long-term clinical trials that establish universal surgical standards, and that failure to improve with conservative treatment alone does not automatically mean surgery is necessary. That's not a reason to avoid surgery when it's warranted — it's a reason to work with a surgeon who takes the diagnostic process seriously and explains the reasoning behind every recommendation.

The biggest predictor of a good outcome isn't which procedure you have — it's whether the procedure is matched to the actual structural cause of your pain.


## What Happens If TMJ Goes Untreated?


For many people, TMJ symptoms are cyclical — they flare, settle, and return. But for others, the condition is progressive. Untreated structural damage to the joint can worsen over time, making later interventions more complex and less likely to fully succeed.

There's also a cost that's harder to quantify. Research published by the National Academies of Sciences found that the largest financial burden of living with TMD isn't medical bills or missed workdays — it's reduced productivity while at work. Patients averaged significantly more days per year at their desks in pain, unable to concentrate or perform at full capacity, compared to those without the condition. That invisible daily tax compounds over time.

The point isn't to alarm anyone into a procedure they're not ready for. It's to be clear that waiting isn't always the neutral option it feels like.


## How to Find the Right Surgeon for TMJ Surgery


TMJ surgery falls within the specialty of oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMS) — the field that trains specifically in the bones, joints, and soft tissues of the jaw and face. When evaluating a surgeon, it's reasonable to ask:

How many TMJ procedures do you perform per year?

Which imaging will be used to guide the surgical plan?

What conservative options have been tried, and why is surgery the recommended next step?

What does your specific post-operative recovery protocol look like?

At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery, our surgeons have been caring for patients throughout West Los Angeles for over 50 years, with a team that spans multiple board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons. If you're at the point where you're seriously evaluating surgery, a consultation is the right next step — not to commit to anything, but to get a clear, honest picture of your options.

Book a consultation and bring your imaging, your history, and your questions. That's exactly what we're here for.


## Frequently Asked Questions About TMJ Surgery


Is TMJ surgery worth it? For the right candidate — someone who has genuinely exhausted conservative options and has confirmed structural joint damage — surgery can be transformative. Long-term studies tracking patients for more than two decades show satisfaction rates above 85%, with lasting reductions in pain, clicking, and jaw locking.

What is the success rate of TMJ surgery? It varies by procedure. Arthroscopic surgery shows long-term success rates of roughly 77–84% across published studies. Total joint replacement, in appropriate end-stage cases, carries a 97% prosthesis survival rate and delivers 75–87% pain reduction, according to a 2025 review of nearly 2,400 patients.

Can TMJ come back after surgery? In some cases, yes — particularly if underlying contributing factors (like bruxism, joint inflammation from arthritis, or bite issues) aren't also addressed. This is why post-surgical care, including physical therapy, occlusal management, and follow-up monitoring, is part of a complete treatment plan, not an afterthought.

Will I need to take a long time off work? For minimally invasive procedures like arthrocentesis or arthroscopy, most patients return to desk work within a few days to a week. Open surgery and total joint replacement require 2–6 weeks of recovery before returning to most professional activities.


## Ready to Understand Your Options?


TMJ pain that hasn't responded to conservative treatment deserves a real evaluation — not more waiting. The surgical options available today, performed by experienced oral and maxillofacial surgeons, have a proven track record of restoring jaw function and quality of life for patients who need them.

If you're in the Santa Monica, Beverly Hills, Los Angeles, or West LA area and want a clear, no-pressure assessment of where you stand, our team is ready to help. Schedule your consultation at Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery and get the answers you've been looking for.

# Santa Monica Sleep Dentistry: A Fear-Free Path to a Perfect Smile


For many patients in Santa Monica and West Los Angeles, dental anxiety can feel like an insurmountable barrier to achieving optimal oral health. If the thought of dental procedures makes your heart race or keeps you awake at night, you're not alone. Sleep dentistry is available for those procedures that make you grit your teeth.

At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we've been pioneering gentle, patient-centered care since 1974. Our advanced sedation dentistry options ensure that even the most anxious patients can receive the oral surgery care they need without fear or discomfort.


## Understanding Sleep Dentistry: More Than Just "Sleeping Through Surgery"


Sleep dentistry, also known as sedation dentistry, encompasses various techniques that help patients achieve deep relaxation or unconsciousness during dental procedures. Despite the name, most "sleep dentistry" doesn't actually involve being fully asleep – rather, it creates a state of profound calm and comfort.


### The Science Behind Dental Anxiety


Dental anxiety affects approximately 36% of the population, with 12% experiencing extreme dental phobia, according to BMC Oral Health. This fear often stems from:

Previous traumatic dental experiences

Fear of pain or discomfort

Feeling of loss of control

Embarrassment about oral health condition

Claustrophobia from dental equipment

When anxiety goes untreated, patients often delay necessary care, leading to more complex problems that require extensive treatment – creating a cycle of fear and deteriorating oral health.


## Comprehensive Sedation Options at Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery


As the longest-established oral surgery practice in West Los Angeles, we offer the full spectrum of sedation options, each carefully selected based on your individual needs, medical history, and the complexity of your procedure.

Our options range in consciousness levels to best suit your needs:

A low level of sedation – you will feel completely relaxed but will not be asleep.

Moderate sedation – you will feel more relaxed, even drowsy and although not fully asleep, you may not remember much afterwards.

Deep sedation – you will wake up easily but will be more or less unconscious.

General anesthesia – you will be fully asleep/unconscious and will not be aware of anything.


### Nitrous Oxide (Laughing Gas)


The mildest form of sedation, nitrous oxide helps patients feel relaxed and euphoric while remaining fully conscious and able to respond to instructions. This option is ideal for:

Minor procedures like single tooth extractions

Patients with mild anxiety

Those who need to drive themselves home after treatment


### Oral Sedation for Dental Work


Oral sedation for dental work involves taking prescribed medication before your appointment. This method offers deeper relaxation than nitrous oxide while allowing patients to remain responsive.

Benefits of oral sedation include:

Convenient pill form taken at home

Amnesia effect – little memory of the procedure

Suitable for longer procedures

Cost-effective option


### IV Sedation: The Gold Standard for Complex Procedures


Intravenous sedation provides the deepest level of conscious sedation available in an outpatient setting. This method is particularly beneficial for:

Wisdom teeth removal

Dental implant surgery

All-on-Four dental implants

Orthognathic (jaw) surgery


### General Anesthesia for Extensive Procedures


For the most complex cases or patients with severe medical conditions, general anesthesia may be recommended. Our board-certified surgeons have hospital privileges and extensive training in anesthesia management, ensuring the highest level of safety.


## The Sleep Dentistry Experience: What to Expect



### Pre-Procedure Consultation


Every sedation case begins with a thorough medical evaluation. Our team reviews:

Complete medical history and current medications

Previous experiences with anesthesia

Anxiety levels and specific concerns

Type and complexity of planned procedure


### Day of Surgery


On the day of your procedure, you'll arrive at our state-of-the-art Santa Monica facility, where our experienced surgical team will:

Pre-operative assessment: Vital signs monitoring and final medical clearance

Sedation administration: Delivery of chosen sedation method with continuous monitoring

Procedure completion: Surgery performed while you rest comfortably

Recovery monitoring: Careful observation as sedation effects wear off


## Safety: Our Top Priority


At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, patient safety drives every decision. Our safety protocols include:

Board-certified surgeons: All our doctors completed accredited residency programs and maintain active hospital privileges

Advanced monitoring: State-of-the-art equipment tracks vital signs throughout procedures

Emergency preparedness: Full resuscitation equipment and emergency protocols

Continuing education: Regular training in the latest safety techniques and protocols


## Who Benefits Most from Sleep Dentistry?


Based on our 50 years of experience serving the Santa Monica community, ideal candidates for sleep dentistry include:


### High-Anxiety Patients


If dental visits cause panic attacks, sweating, or sleepless nights, sedation dentistry can break the cycle of fear and avoidance.


### Complex Procedure Patients


Lengthy procedures like facial trauma reconstruction or full-mouth rehabilitation are more comfortable under sedation.


### Gag Reflex Issues


Patients with sensitive gag reflexes often find sedation allows completion of necessary procedures.


### Time-Conscious Professionals


Busy Santa Monica professionals appreciate that sedation allows multiple procedures in a single appointment, minimizing time away from work.


### Special Needs Patients


Individuals with autism, ADHD, or other conditions that make sitting still difficult benefit greatly from sedation options.


## Addressing Common Concerns About Sleep Dentistry



### "Will I Say Something Embarrassing?"


While some patients experience mild disinhibition, our professional team maintains strict confidentiality and creates a judgment-free environment.


### "What If Something Goes Wrong?"


Our surgeons complete rigorous training in anesthesia management, and our facility maintains full emergency protocols. Complications are extraordinarily rare when procedures are performed by qualified specialists.


### "How Long Will Recovery Take?"


Recovery time varies by sedation type:

Nitrous oxide: Immediate recovery

Oral sedation: 4-6 hours

IV sedation: 6-8 hours

General anesthesia: 12-24 hours


### "Is Sleep Dentistry Covered by Insurance?"


Many insurance plans cover sedation when medically necessary. Our financial coordinators help maximize your benefits and offer flexible payment options.


## Why Choose Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery for Sleep Dentistry?



### Unmatched Experience


As Santa Monica's premier oral surgery practice for 50 years, we've successfully administered thousands of sedation cases with an impeccable safety record.


### Board-Certified Expertise


Every member of our surgical team is board-certified by the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, representing the highest level of training in sedation and anesthesia management.


### State-of-the-Art Technology


Our Santa Monica facility features the latest monitoring equipment and surgical technology, ensuring optimal safety and outcomes.


### Comprehensive Care


From simple extractions to complex reconstructive procedures, our team handles the full spectrum of oral and maxillofacial surgery under one roof.


## Taking the First Step: Your Consultation


Ready to explore how Santa Monica sleep dentistry can transform your experience? Your journey begins with a comprehensive consultation at our Santa Monica facility.

During your visit, we'll:

Discuss your specific concerns and anxiety triggers

Review your medical history and current medications

Explain sedation options appropriate for your needs

Answer all questions about the process and recovery

Create a personalized treatment plan


## Transform Your Dental Experience Today


Don't let fear prevent you from achieving optimal oral health. With our advanced sedation dentistry options and 50 years of trusted expertise, Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants makes even the most complex procedures comfortable and stress-free.

Ready to discover fear-free dentistry? Call (310) 315-1034 to schedule your sedation consultation today.


## Medical Disclaimers and Additional Information


This information is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Individual results may vary based on patient-specific factors. Consult with a board-certified oral surgeon for personalized treatment recommendations. Not all patients are candidates for all sedation methods.

Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants maintains strict HIPAA compliance and patient privacy standards. All sedation procedures are performed in accordance with American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons guidelines.

# Los Angeles Oral Surgery at Santa Monica OMS


When it comes to smiles ready for the spotlight, Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants (Santa Monica OMS) has quietly set the stage behind some of Los Angeles’s most radiant and camera-ready smiles for nearly 50 years. At Santa Monica OMS, oral surgery transcends routine care, it's an exceptional, personalized experience tailored for patients who expect superior outcomes. Guided by board-certified surgeons, advanced technology, and concierge-level care, Santa Monica OMS invites you into an elite circle of patients who trust their smiles to the best in Los Angeles oral surgery. Discover the unparalleled level of skill, precision, and comfort awaiting you at this premier practice.


## Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery in Los Angeles


Santa Monica OMS offers a complete range of oral and maxillofacial procedures under one roof, including dental implants, wisdom-tooth extraction, corrective jaw surgery, bone grafting, sinus lifts, and facial trauma treatments. The state-of-the-art facility features:

Advanced in-house CBCT imaging for detailed 3-D planning

Operating suites accredited to stringent hospital standards

Comprehensive anesthesia options, including local anesthesia, IV sedation, and general anesthesia


## Meet the Surgical Team


Santa Monica OMS’s exceptional reputation stems from its highly credentialed surgical team. Each surgeon holds dual degrees in dentistry (DDS or DMD) and medicine (MD) and is board-certified by the American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.


### Dr. Howard H. Park, DMD, MD


Specializing in dental implants, advanced bone grafting, and "teeth-in-a-day" full-arch restorations. Dr. Park is board-certified and serves on the faculty at UCLA, bringing extensive experience in innovative implant techniques.


### Dr. Richard H. Ting, DDS, MD


Expert in corrective jaw surgery and facial-trauma reconstruction, available for emergency care through local hospitals. Dr. Ting is the Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery department chair at Providence Saint John's Health Center and an anesthesia examiner for the Dental Board of California.


### Dr. Gil B. Ivry, DDS, MD


Focused on TMJ disorders, nerve reconstruction, and prioritizing patient comfort during complex procedures. Dr. Ivry also specializes in treating complex oral pathologies and facial pain syndromes.


### Dr. Jeffrey M. Tanner, DDS, MD


Renowned for minimally invasive wisdom-tooth extractions and ensuring comfortable, smooth recoveries. Dr. Tanner frequently lectures on pain management and is recognized for his patient-focused approach.


### Dr. Derek L. Vajda, DDS, MD


Experienced in managing pathology, complex extractions, and salvage procedures for dental implants. Dr. Vajda also specializes in reconstructive solutions following implant complications, prioritizing long-term dental health.


### Dr. Harry Schwartz, DMD, MD, FACS


Board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon with broad expertise in facial reconstruction, implant dentistry, and surgical treatments for oral pathologies. Dr. Schwartz is recognized as a Fellow of the American College of Surgeons, emphasizing excellence in patient care and surgical outcomes.


## Santa Monica’s Best in Oral Surgery



### Dental Implants and Full-Arch Solutions


The practice offers individual implants, bridges, and innovative All-on-Four® full-arch restorations, utilizing precise guided-surgery techniques for efficiency and accuracy. Comprehensive treatment planning ensures predictable outcomes and tailored solutions for every patient’s unique dental needs.


### Wisdom-Tooth Extraction Under IV Sedation


Impacted or challenging wisdom teeth are comfortably removed in the practice's dedicated surgical suites, ensuring rapid recovery and minimal discomfort. IV sedation provides stress-free procedures, significantly reducing patient anxiety and enhancing overall comfort during surgery.


### Corrective Jaw (Orthognathic) Surgery


The surgical team works alongside orthodontists to treat patients with bite discrepancies, facial asymmetry, and airway concerns, improving both function and aesthetics. Detailed virtual planning and precise surgical execution optimize results and minimize recovery time.


### Sinus-Lift and Bone-Grafting Procedures


Advanced techniques are used to reinforce bone in preparation for implants, ensuring long-lasting stability and successful dental implant placement. Procedures leverage state-of-the-art materials and minimally invasive approaches to maximize patient comfort and healing.


### Comprehensive Anesthesia Care


Each surgeon is fully certified to administer all levels of anesthesia, ensuring patient safety, comfort, and peace of mind throughout every procedure. Continuous monitoring and customized sedation plans guarantee optimal patient relaxation and enhanced surgical experiences.


### Emergency Facial-Trauma & TMJ Management


Santa Monica OMS surgeons provide rapid response to facial trauma and TMJ emergencies, partnering with local hospitals to deliver timely, effective care. Their experience in acute interventions ensures optimal recovery outcomes, restoring patients’ health, comfort, and functionality swiftly.


## What Patients Are Saying


Santa Monica OMS maintains an outstanding 4.8/5-star average across more than 700 online reviews. Patients consistently praise compassionate care, transparent communication, and smooth recoveries:

“Incredibly positive experience! A day after 3 extractions—no pain, no bleeding, and very minimal swelling. Dr. Tanner was highly professional, very engaging, and most importantly, he clearly does excellent work!” – Mark S.

“Dr. Ting explained everything and always ensured I was comfortable. He is gentle and kind, with a great bedside manner. The staff working with him was competent and kind—a well-run team.” – Suzy R.


## World-Class Surgical Center


Accredited operatories meeting hospital-grade sterilization and monitoring standards

State-of-the-art in-house CBCT imaging for precise surgical planning

Comfortable private recovery areas with attentive post-op care, including warm blankets, hydration, and personal monitoring


### Patient-Centered Los Angeles Oral Surgery Services at Santa Monica OMS


Transparent Pricing and Billing:

Santa Monica OMS provides clear, upfront details about treatment costs. Fees are based on procedure complexity and quality care. Payment is required at the time of service, and the office submits claims for patients using out-of-network insurance plans.

Secure Online Patient Registration:

New or returning patients (after two years) can conveniently complete a secure online registration before their appointment, which includes acknowledging privacy and financial policies.

Easy Online Bill Payment:

Patients can quickly and securely pay bills online using the patient reference number provided by the office, simplifying the payment process.


## Frequently Asked Questions



## Q: How long is recovery after wisdom-teeth removal?


A: Most patients resume normal activities within three to four days, though recovery varies based on individual healing and procedure specifics. Swelling and discomfort typically subside significantly within a week.


## Q: Can you get a full set of implants in one day?


A: Yes, in select cases with adequate bone structure, Santa Monica OMS offers advanced full-arch implant solutions such as "teeth-in-a-day." Your surgeon will evaluate your candidacy during the consultation using CBCT imaging.


## Q: Do you accept PPO insurance?


A: Yes. The office assists with insurance pre-authorization and clearly outlines any expected out-of-pocket costs upfront.


## Q: What financing is available?


A: Flexible financing options, including interest-free promotional periods through CareCredit®, are available to help manage the cost of treatment.


## Q: What should I expect during my first consultation?


A: Your initial consultation involves a thorough examination, CBCT imaging if necessary, and a detailed discussion of treatment options, costs, and expected outcomes. This visit is designed to ensure clarity and comfort about your treatment plan.


## Q: Is sedation dentistry safe?


A: Absolutely. Our team includes board-certified surgeons trained in advanced anesthesia techniques. Continuous monitoring ensures your safety and comfort throughout any sedation procedure.


## Take the Next Step Toward Your Best Smile


Whether you seek a single dental implant or comprehensive Los Angeles oral surgery solutions, Santa Monica OMS provides world-class, personalized care designed to meet the highest standards. To arrange your consultation, call 310-315-1034 or book an appointment online now.

# Beverly Hills Oral Surgery by Santa Monica OMS: Your Path to a Confident Smile


Facing oral surgery can feel like a big deal—maybe you’re nervous about pain or just want to smile without thinking twice. At Santa Monica Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (OMS), we’re here to take the stress out of it. Our Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants is all about making you feel comfortable while creating a smile you’re proud of. Our Beverly Hills oral & facial surgeons are experts in tooth implants in, wisdom tooth removal, and more, working closely with you to build a plan that feels right. Let’s explore how we can help you shine.


## Services That Put You First


Surgery isn’t just about fixing teeth—it’s about getting back to being you. We focus on what matters to you, offering procedures that blend skill with care:

Wisdom Teeth Removal: We keep it quick and gentle, so you’re back to your routine with minimal discomfort.

Jaw Surgery: Struggling with a misaligned bite or jaw pain? We realign things to help you eat, talk, and feel better.

TMJ Relief: Jaw pain or clicking driving you nuts? Our treatments ease the ache and restore smooth movement.

# Preparing for Your Oral Surgery: Essential Pre-Operative and Post-Operative Care Tips


Oral surgery is an important step toward improved oral health, but its success hinges on thorough preparation and diligent recovery care. At Santa Monica OMS, we blend advanced technology with personalized care to ensure every patient experiences a safe procedure and a smooth, comfortable recovery. Below are key tips to help you prepare for your surgery and maintain optimal healing afterward.


## Pre-Operative Care: Laying the Foundation


Comprehensive Consultation: Meet with our board‑certified oral surgeons to discuss your medical history, current medications, and any concerns. This detailed evaluation allows us to create a customized treatment plan that minimizes risks.

Personalized Treatment Planning: We develop a plan tailored to your unique dental structure and health needs, ensuring that every aspect of your procedure—from anesthesia to surgical technique—is optimized for you.

Medication Management: Follow specific instructions regarding medication adjustments. For example, if you’re taking blood thinners, our team will advise you on temporary discontinuation to reduce bleeding risks.

Fasting and Preparation Guidelines: Adhere strictly to fasting instructions (usually an eight‑hour fast) to prevent complications related to anesthesia. Preparing your home in advance with soft foods and a comfortable recovery area is also recommended.

Before Intravenous Anesthesia Sedation: You may not have anything to eat or drink (including water) for eight hours before the appointment. Click here for the full list of advanced instructions before intravenous anesthesia sedation.

Logistics and Transportation: Arrange for a trusted companion to drive you home post-surgery, as the effects of anesthesia can impair your ability to drive safely.


## Post-Operative Care: Promoting a Smooth Recovery


Managing Discomfort and Bleeding: It’s normal to experience minor bleeding and discomfort after oral surgery. Follow your surgeon’s post-operative care instructions for pain management and gently bite on gauze to control bleeding. Use ice packs intermittently (20 minutes on, 10 minutes off) during the first 48 hours to reduce swelling.

Maintaining Oral Hygiene: Continue to care for your mouth by gently rinsing with a warm saltwater solution (after the first 24 hours) while avoiding the surgical site. This helps keep the area clean and promotes healing.

Dietary Adjustments: Start with clear liquids and soft foods, such as soups and mashed potatoes. Gradually reintroduce solid foods as healing progresses, but avoid hot, spicy, or crunchy foods that could irritate the surgical area.

Activity and Rest: Rest is critical post-surgery. Avoid strenuous activities for several days to prevent complications like increased bleeding or swelling. Follow our specific guidelines regarding when it’s safe to resume your normal routine.

Follow-Up Appointments: Schedule follow-up visits with our team to monitor your recovery, address any concerns, and adjust your care plan if necessary. Continuous support is essential for ensuring a long-lasting, successful outcome.


## Your Next Steps


Your oral surgery experience should be as smooth and comfortable as possible. At Santa Monica OMS, we are dedicated to providing exceptional care every step of the way—from your initial consultation to your final follow-up appointment. If you’re preparing for oral surgery, take control of your recovery by following these essential care tips. Our expert team is here to support you before, during, and after your procedure, ensuring you achieve optimal healing and long-term oral health.

Our board‑certified surgeons and state‑of‑the‑art facility deliver personalized, compassionate care for patients throughout Santa Monica, Culver City, and beyond. We specialize in a wide range of procedures—from wisdom tooth extractions to dental implants—ensuring every patient receives exceptional treatment and lasting results.

# All-on-Four Dental Implants in Santa Monica, CA: A Comprehensive Guide


When it comes to restoring your smile, All-on-Four dental implants offer a breakthrough solution that combines advanced technology with proven results. At Santa Monica OMS, we specialize in full arch dental implants that provide a permanent, natural-looking restoration for patients in Santa Monica, Culver City, and the surrounding neighborhoods.


## What Are All-on-Four Dental Implants?


All-on-Four dental implants are designed to support an entire arch of replacement teeth using just four strategically placed implants. This innovative approach reduces the need for bone grafting and allows for a more streamlined procedure compared to traditional implant methods. At Santa Monica OMS, our full arch dental implants are carefully planned to restore not only your dental function but also your confidence.


## Key Benefits of All-on-Four Dental Implants



### Enhanced Functionality and Stability


All-on-Four implants offer superior stability, mimicking the natural bite and improving chewing efficiency. Patients enjoy the freedom to eat a wider variety of foods without the worries associated with removable dentures. Our expert team in Santa Monica ensures that each implant is precisely placed for maximum function and durability.


### Natural Aesthetics and Increased Confidence


One of the most appealing benefits of All-on-Four dental implants is their natural appearance. The implants are designed to blend seamlessly with your existing teeth, providing a flawless smile that boosts self-esteem. This benefit is especially valued by patients in Santa Monica and neighboring Culver City, where aesthetic appeal is a top priority.


### Minimally Invasive Procedure and Faster Recovery


By using only four implants per arch, the procedure is less invasive and typically requires a shorter recovery time than traditional methods. This means you can return to your daily routine in Santa Monica, or even if you live in nearby Culver City, much faster—with minimal discomfort and downtime.


### Long-Term Durability and Cost-Effectiveness


Although the initial investment in All-on-Four dental implants may be higher than other options, their longevity and low maintenance needs make them a cost-effective solution over time. Patients experience a significant reduction in repair or replacement costs, and the durability of these implants ensures you enjoy a stable, lasting smile.

## Understanding Sedation Dentistry Options


The fear of dental procedures affects countless individuals in our community, often leading to delayed treatment and worsening oral health conditions. At our Santa Monica practice, we've developed comprehensive sedation protocols that address varying levels of anxiety and procedure complexity. Our approach combines years of clinical expertise with the latest advances in sedation dentistry to ensure both comfort and safety.

Modern sedation techniques have revolutionized the field of oral surgery, making even the most complex procedures manageable for anxious patients. Through careful evaluation of each patient's medical history, anxiety level, and procedure requirements, we create personalized sedation plans that provide optimal comfort while maintaining the highest safety standards.

Our comprehensive sedation options include:

Nitrous oxide sedation for mild anxiety

Oral conscious sedation for moderate procedures

IV sedation for complex surgical treatments

Local anesthesia for precise pain control

Monitored care throughout your procedure

Modern sedation dentistry represents a breakthrough in patient care, particularly for those who have postponed treatment due to anxiety. In our Santa Monica practice, we've witnessed countless success stories where appropriate sedation has enabled patients to receive necessary care comfortably. The impact extends beyond the procedure itself, often transforming patients' entire perspective on dental treatment.

Our experience has shown that when patients feel secure in their sedation choice, they're more likely to maintain regular dental care and address oral health issues promptly. This proactive approach leads to better overall outcomes and can prevent more complex problems from developing.

Reduced anxiety and stress

Comprehensive safety protocols

Wisdom teeth extraction

Modern monitoring systems and emergency preparedness equipment ensure we're ready for any situation. Our surgical suites combine comfort with clinical excellence, creating an ideal environment for sedation procedures.

Modern patient amenities

Your recovery begins in our monitored care area and continues with careful attention to your progress at home. We maintain contact throughout your recovery period to ensure optimal healing and comfort.

# Say Goodbye to TMJ Pain: The Power of Early Detection and Treatment


Are you experiencing jaw pain, clicking sounds when you eat, or headaches that just won’t go away? These could be early signs of a temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorder. At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we believe that catching TMJ issues early is your ticket to a pain-free smile. Let’s dive into why early detection is crucial and how it can help you find relief faster.


#### Spotting TMJ Troubles Early: Your First Step to Freedom


TMJ disorders can sneak up on you, often starting with subtle symptoms that are easy to brush off. But recognizing these early warning signs can make all the difference:

Jaw pain or tenderness

Clicking or popping sounds when opening your mouth

Difficulty or discomfort while chewing

Facial pain or recurring headaches

Jaw locking or limited movement

If you’re nodding along to any of these, it’s time to take action. Early detection isn’t just about identifying a problem – it’s about opening the door to quicker, more effective treatment.


#### Why Acting Fast on TMJ Disorders is a Game-Changer


Nip Pain in the Bud: Catch it early, and you can often stop pain from becoming your constant companion.

Keep It Simple: Early-stage TMJ often responds well to conservative treatments, helping you avoid more complex procedures down the road.

Save Time and Money: Addressing TMJ issues promptly typically means faster relief and can be more cost-effective than treating advanced cases.

Protect Your Smile: Early intervention can prevent TMJ disorders from affecting your bite or causing wear on your teeth.

Boost Your Quality of Life: Don’t let jaw pain hold you back from enjoying your favorite foods or flashing your biggest smile.


#### Our Approach: Tailored TMJ Care for Lasting Relief


At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we don’t believe in one-size-fits-all solutions. Our approach to TMJ treatment is as unique as you are:

Comprehensive evaluation to pinpoint the root cause of your TMJ issues

Customized treatment plans that may include physical therapy, oral appliances, or minimally invasive procedures

Cutting-edge diagnostic tools for accurate assessment

Expert care from specialists who understand the complexities of TMJ disorders


#### Did You Know? TMJ and Wisdom Teeth: An Unexpected Connection


Interestingly, TMJ pain can sometimes be linked to other dental issues, including wisdom teeth problems. In some cases, the pressure from impacted wisdom teeth can contribute to jaw discomfort. If you’re experiencing persistent jaw pain, it’s crucial to have a thorough evaluation, which may include assessing your wisdom teeth. Learn more about wisdom teeth removal and how it might affect your jaw health.


#### Take the First Step Towards a Pain-Free Jaw


Don’t let TMJ pain become your new normal. Early detection and treatment can put you on the fast track to relief. If you’re experiencing any signs of TMJ disorders, it’s time to take action.

Learn more about your first visit and what to expect when you come to our office. We’re here to make your journey to jaw health as smooth and comfortable as possible.

# Wisdom Teeth Removal Recovery: Essential Post-Operative Care Guide


Wisdom teeth extraction is a common oral surgery procedure, typically performed between ages 17-25. At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we understand that proper post-operative care is crucial for a smooth recovery. This guide will walk you through essential steps to ensure optimal healing after your wisdom teeth removal.


## Understanding the Recovery Process


Recovery from wisdom teeth extraction usually takes a few days to a week. Most patients can return to normal activities within a week, but following proper care instructions is vital for preventing complications and ensuring comfort.


### What to Expect Immediately After Surgery


Mild swelling and discomfort are normal

Some bleeding may occur for the first 24 hours

You may experience limited jaw opening


## Essential Post-Operative Care Tips



### 1. Rest and Activity Limitation


Rest for the remainder of the day after surgery

Avoid strenuous activities for at least 2-3 days

Gradually return to normal activities as you feel comfortable


### 2. Managing Swelling and Discomfort


Apply ice packs to the cheeks in 20-minute intervals for the first 24 hours

After 24 hours, switch to warm compresses to promote healing

Take prescribed pain medication as directed by your oral surgeon


### 3. Proper Oral Hygiene


Avoid brushing the surgical area for the first 24 hours

After 24 hours, gently rinse with warm salt water 2-3 times daily

Continue brushing other teeth normally, being careful around the extraction sites


### 4. Diet and Nutrition


Stick to soft foods for the first few days (e.g., yogurt, smoothies, mashed potatoes)

Avoid hot liquids and alcoholic beverages for at least 24 hours

Do not use straws for at least a week to prevent dry socket


### 5. Avoiding Complications


Don’t smoke for at least 72 hours after surgery

Avoid touching the surgical area with your tongue or fingers

If stitches were used, they typically dissolve on their own within 7-10 days


## When to Contact Your Oral Surgeon


While some discomfort is normal, contact Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants if you experience:

Excessive bleeding that doesn’t subside

Severe pain not relieved by prescribed medication

Signs of infection (fever, excessive swelling, pus)

Persistent numbness or tingling


## FAQs About Wisdom Teeth Removal Recovery


Q: How long does it take for the extraction site to fully heal?

A: Complete healing typically takes 3-4 weeks, although the initial recovery is much shorter.

Q: When can I resume exercise after wisdom teeth removal?

A: Light exercise can usually be resumed after 3-4 days, but avoid strenuous activities for at least a week.

Q: Is it normal to have bad breath after wisdom teeth extraction?

A: Some bad breath is normal for a few days post-surgery. Proper oral hygiene and salt water rinses can help.

Q: How soon can I eat solid foods after the surgery?

A: Most patients can return to a normal diet within a week, but start with soft foods and gradually introduce solids as comfort allows.

With over 40 years of experience in oral and maxillofacial surgery, our team at Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants is committed to providing exceptional care. Dr. Kimia Bagheri and our other skilled surgeons ensure that each patient receives personalized attention and the highest standard of treatment.

Our practice’s deep roots in the Santa Monica community, combined with our state-of-the-art techniques, make us the trusted choice for wisdom teeth extraction and other oral surgery procedures.

# Corrective Jaw Surgery Benefits: Transform Your Life, Restore Your Smile


At Santa MonicaCenter for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we believe that everyone deserves a smile that not only looks great but functions perfectly. Corrective jaw surgery, also known as orthognathic surgery, can be a life-changing procedure for many of our patients. Let’s explore how this transformative surgery can benefit you, both aesthetically and functionally.


## Understanding Corrective Jaw Surgery


Corrective jaw surgery is a specialized procedure designed to realign the jaws and teeth to improve both function and appearance. It’s not just about creating a beautiful smile – it’s about restoring proper jaw function, enhancing overall oral health, and boosting your confidence.


## The Life-Changing Benefits of Corrective Jaw Surgery


1. Improved Bite and Chewing Function

One of the primary corrective jaw surgery benefits is the significant improvement in bite alignment and chewing function. Patients often experience:

More efficient and comfortable chewing

Reduced strain on jaw muscles and joints

Improved digestion due to better food breakdown

2. Enhanced Facial Appearance

Corrective jaw surgery can dramatically transform your facial profile, leading to:

Balanced facial proportions

Correction of underbites, overbites, or asymmetry

A more defined chin and jawline

3. Breathing and Sleep Improvements

Many patients report significant improvements in breathing and sleep quality after surgery, including:

Reduced snoring and sleep apnea symptoms

Improved airway function

Better overall sleep quality

4. Speech Enhancement

Jaw misalignment can affect speech patterns. Corrective surgery often results in:

Clearer pronunciation

Improved ability to form certain sounds

Increased confidence in verbal communication

5. Relief from TMJ Disorders

For those suffering from temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders, corrective jaw surgery can provide:

Reduced jaw pain and discomfort

Decreased headaches and facial pain

Improved jaw mobility

6. Boost in Self-Confidence

Perhaps one of the most significant benefits is the boost in self-esteem and confidence that comes with a transformed smile and improved facial aesthetics.


## Our Approach: Expertise Meets Compassion


At Santa MonicaCenter for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we understand that the decision to undergo corrective jaw surgery is significant. That’s why we approach each case with a combination of surgical expertise and genuine care for our patients’ well-being. Our team is committed to:

Providing comprehensive evaluations to determine the best treatment plan

Using state-of-the-art technology for precise surgical planning and execution

# All-on-Four Dental Implants: Your Same-Day Smile Transformation in Santa Monica


Are you tired of living with missing teeth or struggling with uncomfortable dentures? Imagine regaining your confident smile and enjoying your favorite foods again in just one day. With All-on-Four dental implants, this dream can become a reality.


## What are All-on-Four Dental Implants?


All-on-Four is a revolutionary dental implant procedure that can replace an entire arch of missing teeth using just four strategically placed implants. This innovative technique offers a permanent, stable, and natural-looking solution for those who have experienced significant tooth loss.


### How Does It Work?


The All-on-Four procedure involves the following steps:

Consultation and Planning: Your oral surgeon will assess your oral health, bone density, and overall medical condition to determine if you’re a suitable candidate for All-on-Four.

Implant Placement: During a single surgical procedure, four dental implants are strategically placed in your jawbone.

Temporary Bridge Attachment: A temporary set of teeth is attached to the implants on the same day, allowing you to leave with a brand-new smile.

Healing and Integration: Over the next few months, the implants will fuse with your jawbone, providing a strong and stable foundation for your permanent teeth.

Permanent Prosthesis Placement: Once the implants have fully integrated, your oral surgeon will replace the temporary bridge with a custom-designed, permanent prosthesis that looks and feels like natural teeth.


### Why Choose All-on-Four?


All-on-Four dental implants offer numerous advantages over traditional dentures and implant methods:

Immediate Results: You’ll leave the office with a new smile on the same day as your surgery.

Minimally Invasive: The procedure requires fewer implants and often eliminates the need for bone grafting.

Enhanced Stability: The four implants provide a secure foundation for your new teeth, preventing slippage and discomfort.

Improved Function: You can eat, speak, and laugh with confidence, just like you would with natural teeth.

Long-Term Solution: With proper care, All-on-Four implants can last a lifetime.

Natural-Looking Results: Your new teeth will be custom-designed to blend seamlessly with your facial features.


## Meet Our Expert Surgeons


At Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, our team of highly skilled and experienced oral surgeons is dedicated to providing you with the highest quality care. Dr. Howard Park, Dr. Richard Ting, Dr. Gil Ivry, Dr. Jeffrey Tanner, and Dr. Derek Vajda are all board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeons with extensive experience in dental implant procedures. They are committed to staying at the forefront of dental implant technology and techniques to ensure you receive the best possible results.


## Your All-on-Four Journey Begins Today


If you’re ready to transform your smile and regain your confidence, All-on-Four dental implants may be the perfect solution for you. Contact the experienced team at Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants today to schedule a consultation and learn more about this life-changing procedure. We’ll provide personalized care and guide you through every step of your All-on-Four journey, helping you achieve the smile of your dreams.

Contact us today to schedule a consultation and take the first step towards a confident, radiant smile and renewed quality of life.

# Unveiling the Smile: Exploring Cutting-Edge Oral Surgery in the Heart of Los Angeles


Los Angeles is a city where a beautiful smile can open doors. If you’re searching for expert Los Angeles oral surgery providers to address dental problems or enhance your smile’s brilliance, it’s time to discover the remarkable world of modern oral surgery. Santa Monica Center for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (also known as Santa Monica OMS) can help!


## The Scope of Oral Surgery


Oral and maxillofacial surgery encompasses far more than tooth extractions. Highly trained oral surgeons specialize in a wide range of procedures, including:

Wisdom Teeth Removal: Proactive removal of impacted or problematic wisdom teeth to maintain your oral health.

Dental Implants: The premier solution for replacing missing teeth, offering a natural look, feel, and function.

Corrective Jaw Surgery: Addresses bite problems, sleep apnea, and facial imbalances for improved health and aesthetics.

Facial Trauma Treatment: Expert reconstruction and rehabilitation following accidents or injuries.

Bone Grafting: Regenerative procedures to prepare the jawbone for dental implants and other treatments.

TMJ Treatment: Relief from pain and dysfunction of the jaw joint (TMJ) through various therapies and, when necessary, surgical solutions.


# Why Choose Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery?


Los Angeles is a center of innovation in oral surgery, offering patients significant advantages:

Advanced Surgical Techniques: Minimally invasive approaches reduce discomfort and promote faster recovery.

Precision Imaging: 3D digital imaging (like CBCT scans) ensures detailed surgical planning for optimal results.

Anesthesia Options: Tailored solutions for maximum comfort and relaxation during procedures.

Collaborative Care: Oral surgeons work seamlessly with your dentist and other specialists to address complex needs.


## Los Angeles Oral Surgery Specialists: Santa Monica Center for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery


At Santa Monica Center for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (also known as Santa Monica OMS), we’re proud of our deep roots in the Los Angeles community. Founded in 1975, we’re the longest-established OMS practice in West Los Angeles. Our commitment to patient-centered care, compassion, and technological innovation remains unwavering. And it shows – we’re humbled to have multiple 5-star profiles with over 700 reviews on Google, a testament to the exceptional experiences our patients have had.


## Meet Our Exceptional Team


At the Santa Monica Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants, we’re not just about fancy technology – it’s our team that makes the difference. Get to know the skilled and compassionate oral surgeons who will be transforming your smile:

Dr. Howard Park: Harvard grad, former UCLA faculty, and all-around brilliant surgeon who specializes in dental implants and complex reconstruction.

Dr. Richard Ting: This guy is the expert in jaw surgery and TMJ disorders– he literally changes lives!

Dr. Gil Ivry: With a background in histology, Dr. Ivry combines precision with a passion for patient comfort and optimal outcomes.

Dr. Jeffrey Tanner: Inspired by his small-town dentist father, Dr. Tanner brings Kansas City warmth and a strong work ethic to his expertise in orthognathic surgery. He’s passionate about serving the LA community and enjoys outdoor adventures with his family.

Dr. Derek Vajda: A proud Chicagoan and dedicated UCLA faculty, Dr. Vajda excels in the full scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery, including complex trauma cases.


## Why Board-Certification Matters


We know it sounds fancy, but board-certified surgeons are a big deal. It means they went above and beyond after their degrees with extra training and rigorous exams. Basically, it means you’re getting care from someone who’s committed to being at the top of their game.


# Let’s Talk About Your Needs


We understand that every patient has unique goals and concerns. Our team will listen carefully to your individual situation and work with you to develop a personalized treatment plan.


# FAQ: Your Oral Surgery Questions Answered


Will my oral surgery be painful? Modern anesthesia and pain management techniques prioritize your comfort throughout the process.

How long is the recovery time? This varies depending on the procedure, but advancements in techniques promote faster healing.

Will my insurance cover oral surgery? Many insurance plans offer coverage. Our team can assist with verifying your benefits.


## Transform Your Smile, Enhance Your Well-being


If you’re ready to explore the benefits of Los Angeles oral surgery and how the experts at Santa Monica Center for Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery can change your smile and overall well-being, contact us today (310) 315-1034. Let us help you unveil the brilliance and confidence a healthy smile brings!
